title: Approved Root Edits are executed by the Operational Facilitator, who also records outcomes for rejected proposals
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.5 gives execution to the reviewer: "at the conclusion of the poll, if the proposal is approved, the Operational Facilitator submits the edit to Powerhouse to formally update the Agent Artifact. Regardless of the outcome, the Operational Facilitator updates the Powerhouse System to include the result of the vote, including any pertinent documents."

So the vote is not self-executing. There is no contract that writes the Artifact when a Snapshot poll passes; a human role transcribes the outcome into the canonical document. Combined with the same role's pre-vote alignment veto, the Facilitator stands at both ends of the amendment pipeline.

The counterweight in this clause is the record-keeping duty, and specifically the words "regardless of the outcome." Failed and rejected proposals are logged with their supporting documents, which means the Facilitator cannot make an inconvenient proposal disappear by simply not acting — an unexecuted approval is visible as a gap between a recorded result and an unchanged Artifact.

That makes auditability the primary enforcement mechanism for a step that has no mechanical enforcement. It works only if someone reads the record.
description: Tokenholders never touch the Artifact: after the poll the Facilitator submits the edit to Powerhouse, and must log the vote result and pertinent documents regardless of whether it passed.
